title: Rotate Image
oneLinerQuestion: Rotate an n x n 2D matrix by 90 degrees clockwise in-place.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Rotate Image problem requires rotating an N x N 2D matrix by 90 degrees clockwise directly in place without allocating a second matrix. A 90-degree clockwise rotation maps an element at matrix[row][col] to matrix[col][N - 1 - row]. Rather than performing complex four-way cyclic coordinate shifts, this geometric transformation can be decomposed into two fundamental linear algebra operations: transposing the matrix along its main diagonal, followed by horizontally reflecting (reversing) each row.

- Step 1: Matrix Transposition Concept — Transposing a square matrix swaps its rows with its columns across the primary diagonal (from top-left to bottom-right). This means every element at index pair (i, j) exchanges positions with (j, i).

- Step 2: In-Place Transposition Traversal — We iterate with an outer loop index 'i' from 0 to N - 1, and an inner loop index 'j' starting from 'i + 1' to N - 1. Restricting 'j' to values strictly greater than 'i' prevents double-swapping elements back to their original locations. Inside the loop, we swap: [matrix[i][j], matrix[j][i]] = [matrix[j][i], matrix[i][j]].

- Step 3: Row Reversal Concept — After transposition, the column elements are correctly grouped into rows, but their horizontal order is mirrored relative to a clockwise turn. Reversing each row horizontally places each column into its final rotated index position.

- Step 4: In-Place Row Reversal Execution — We iterate through each row 'i' from 0 to N - 1. For each row, we apply a standard two-pointer reversal between columns 'left = 0' and 'right = N - 1': while left < right, we swap matrix[i][left] and matrix[i][right], then increment left++ and decrement right--.

- Step 5: Termination & In-Place Verification — After both phases conclude, the matrix has been modified in place to reflect a complete 90-degree clockwise rotation without creating any supplementary 2D buffers.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(N^2) where N is the matrix dimension, as transposition touches N*(N - 1)/2 pairs and reversal touches N*(N / 2) pairs. Space Complexity: O(1) auxiliary space since all coordinate modifications are performed strictly in place using scalar swap variables.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION rotate(matrix):
    n = LENGTH(matrix)
    FOR i FROM 0 TO n - 1 DO:
        FOR j FROM i TO n - 1 DO:
            SWAP(matrix[i][j], matrix[j][i])
        END FOR
    END FOR
    FOR i FROM 0 TO n - 1 DO:
        REVERSE(matrix[i])
    END FOR
END FUNCTION
